papers.title: Bending strength and hardness comparison of titanium and cobalt–chromium alloys for dentures made by selective laser melting
papers.abstract: This in vitro study presents new comparative results for titanium alloy (Ti6Al4V) and cobalt-chromium alloy (Co-Cr) used in removable dental prostheses, including the 3-point bending test and microhardness. For the 3-point bending test, two groups of specimens were designated as group Ti6Al4V and group Co-Cr. For each group, 10 specimens with dimensions of 0.5 × 3 × 25 mm according to ISO 9693-1 were prepared. The Micro-Vickers hardness was measured for 6 specimens of each alloy, with a cylindrical shape (approximately 10 mm in diameter and 3 mm in height). Specimens were prepared with a selective laser melting system for selective laser melting alloys. Different grading of silicon carbide (SiC) papers was used to polish the prepared samples. The surface contaminants were cleaned ultrasonically with acetone and deionized water for at least 10 min. Data were analyzed using Welsh and Mann-Whitney U tests (α = 0.05). No difference in stress values was detected between groups (P = 0.087). However, Ti6Al4V showed higher strain lower modulus of elasticity, and lower microhardness (P < 0.05).

summary_zh.motivation: 比较SLM制备的Ti6Al4V和Co-Cr合金用于义齿的弯曲强度和硬度。
summary_zh.method: 进行三点弯曲试验和显微硬度测试，采用统计检验分析数据。

summary_en.motivation: This study aims to compare the bending strength and hardness of Ti6Al4V and Co-Cr alloys fabricated by selective laser melting for removable dental prostheses.
summary_en.method: Three-point bending tests following ISO 9693-1 and Micro-Vickers hardness measurements were performed, with statistical analysis using Welsh and Mann-Whitney U tests.
summary_en.result: Ti6Al4V exhibited higher strain, lower modulus of elasticity, and lower microhardness than Co-Cr, but no significant difference in stress was found.
summary_en.validation: Validation was conducted through standardized in vitro mechanical testing with ten bending specimens and six hardness specimens per alloy.

papers.title: High-Cycle Fatigue Strength Prediction Model for Ti-6Al-4V Titanium Alloy Compressor Blades Subjected to Foreign Object Damage
papers.abstract: The high-cycle fatigue (HCF) strength of titanium alloy blades, particularly Ti-6Al-4V, is critical for the reliability and performance of aviation engine components. Foreign object damage (FOD), which introduces notches, microstructural alterations, and residual stresses, significantly degrades the fatigue performance of these blades. Of particular concern are tensile residual stresses, which, caused by factors such as FOD, notches, or non-uniform plastic deformation, lead to increased local tensile loads, promote crack initiation, and accelerate crack growth. This study investigates the effects of external damage, including the impact angle and the resultant residual stresses, on the high-cycle fatigue strength of Ti-6Al-4V titanium alloy blades. Blade simulation specimens with impact-induced damage were tested under high-cycle fatigue conditions to assess the influence of various impact angles and the resulting tensile residual stresses. A modified fatigue strength prediction model was developed, incorporating shear factors and tensile residual stresses, to improve the accuracy of fatigue life predictions. Compared with the Neuber model and Peterson model, the modified model increases the proportion of predictions falling within the 10% scatter band by 30%, resulting in a significant improvement in prediction accuracy. The experimental results demonstrated that the modified model more accurately predicted the high-cycle fatigue strength, particularly in the presence of external damage and tensile residual stresses.

summary_en.motivation: To improve the accuracy of high-cycle fatigue strength predictions for Ti-6Al-4V compressor blades damaged by foreign objects.
summary_en.method: Impact tests at various angles were conducted on blade simulation specimens, followed by high-cycle fatigue experiments, and a modified fatigue strength prediction model incorporating shear factors and tensile residual stresses was developed.
summary_en.result: The modified model increased the proportion of predictions within the 10% scatter band by 30% compared to Neuber and Peterson models.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation was performed through high-cycle fatigue testing of impacted blade simulation specimens.

papers.title: Integrating soft computing approach to optimize and predict powder mixed wire electric discharge machinability characteristics of PBLF-Ti-6Al-4V alloy
papers.abstract: This study focuses on optimizing Powder Mixed Wire Electric Discharge Machining of titanium alloy Ti-6Al-4V using zinc, molybdenum disulfide, and carbon nanotubes as dielectric additives. Experiments were designed using Taguchi’s method with analysis of variance to examine the effects of discharge current, pulse on time, gap voltage, and powder concentration on material removal rate, surface roughness, and microhardness. The comparative evaluation of different dielectric powders highlights their distinct roles in improving machining efficiency. The minimum wire weight loss of 0.0049 milligrams per minute was achieved with one gram per litre of zinc, a discharge current of four amperes, a gap voltage of ninety volts, a pulse on time of three hundred milliseconds, and a pulse off time of twenty-five milliseconds. Molybdenum disulfide at one gram per litre produced the highest microhardness of three hundred and sixty-eight Vickers under optimized conditions of four amperes discharge current, one hundred and ten volts gap voltage, two hundred milliseconds pulse on time, and fifty milliseconds pulse off time. Discharge current was found to have the greatest influence on material removal rate, followed by powder concentration. The study provides valuable insights into enhancing machining precision and achieving high-quality performance in titanium alloy applications.

summary_en.motivation: To optimize the powder mixed wire electric discharge machining (PMWEDM) performance of Ti-6Al-4V alloy by investigating the effects of process parameters and dielectric powders.
summary_en.method: Taguchi design of experiments and analysis of variance were used to evaluate the influence of discharge current, pulse on time, gap voltage, and powder concentration on material removal rate, surface roughness, and microhardness.
summary_en.result: Minimum wire weight loss of 0.0049 mg/min was achieved with zinc powder; maximum microhardness of 368 HV was achieved with molybdenum disulfide.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation via Taguchi-optimized trials and ANOVA.

papers.title: SURFACE MORPHOLOGY AND ROUGHNESS EVALUATION OF TITANIUM TREATED WITH MECHANICAL AND CHEMICAL PRE-TREATMENT METHODS
papers.abstract: This study investigates the impact of various mechanical and acid-based pre-treatment techniques on the surface morphology and roughness of Titanium Grade V (Ti-6Al-4V) alloy in order to enhance its fibre adhesion capabilities in metal-fibre composites. Mechanical treatments like sandblasting and copper blasting, single and dual acid etching methods, as well as the combined effects, were systematically examined. For measuring surface roughness, the Mitutoyo portable surface roughness tester and for morphological changes observed by Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) are used. Results showed that Sandblasting and copper blasting increased roughness from 0.27[Formula: see text] [Formula: see text]m (untreated) to 2.87[Formula: see text] [Formula: see text]m ((≈11 times) and 5.65[Formula: see text] [Formula: see text]m ((≈21 times), respectively, while further acid etching on sandblasted specimens enhanced roughness up to 3.69[Formula: see text] [Formula: see text]m ((≈14 times). Dual acid etching methods exhibited variable effects depending on the acid sequence and composition. The study concludes that copper blasting offers the highest enhancement in roughness, whereas the combination of sandblasting followed by dual acid etching yields a balanced surface morphology favorable for strong fiber bonding. These findings provide practical insights into tailoring titanium surface treatments for improved composite performance.

summary_zh.motivation: 通过机械和化学预处理提高钛合金表面粗糙度以增强纤维粘附性。
summary_zh.method: 采用喷砂、铜喷砂、单双酸蚀刻及其组合处理Ti-6Al-4V表面。
summary_zh.result: 铜喷砂使粗糙度从0.27μm增至5.65μm，喷砂后双酸蚀刻实现平衡表面形貌。

summary_en.motivation: To enhance fiber adhesion in metal-fiber composites by modifying the surface roughness of Ti-6Al-4V alloy through mechanical and chemical pre-treatments.
summary_en.method: Systematically evaluated sandblasting, copper blasting, single and dual acid etching, and their combinations on Ti-6Al-4V surfaces.
summary_en.result: Copper blasting achieved the highest roughness increase (21x), while sandblasting followed by dual acid etching provided a balanced morphology for bonding.
summary_en.validation: Surface roughness measured with a Mitutoyo portable tester and morphology observed by SEM.
